extDescription.message: Fills forms with valid Brazilian fake data: CPF, CNPJ, CEP, phone, name and address, as one coherent person.

commandFill.message: Fill the form on the current page

contextMenuFill.message: Fill this form with fake data

popupPick.message: Map a field by clicking it

popupCannotRun.message: Could not run on this page.

optionsAllowedLead.message: One hostname per line. A leading `*.` matches subdomains but not the bare domain, so widening the scope stays deliberate. The point is to stop a stray shortcut from typing a fake CPF into a real signup.

optionsEnforce.message: Only fill forms on the sites listed above

optionsFloatingLead.message: A button on top of the page, to fill without leaving the form. Appearing on its own needs your permission to access the allowed sites above — the same ones where filling was already permitted. Addresses Chrome cannot match, such as `[::1]`, are left out of the button and keep working through the shortcut and the popup.

optionsFloatingToggle.message: Show the floating button on the allowed sites

optionsFloatingDenied.message: Without access to the sites the button cannot appear.

optionsFloatingNoHosts.message: No allowed site Chrome can match — save at least one hostname first.

floatingLabel.message: Fill the form · drag to move · right-click maps a field

optionsMappingsLead.message: When a form hides its labels inside components, detection has nothing to read. Map those fields by hand, one per line:

optionsMappingsHint.message: The URL matches host and path prefix, a port is optional, and `*.` works on the host. Use `skip` as the field to leave a control alone. Mappings win over detection.

optionsMappingsConsole.message: Quicker: use the click-to-map button in the popup. The page console also lists a ready-made selector for every field that was not recognised.

pickerHint.message: Click a field to map it · Esc to leave

optionsLanguageLead.message: The extension ships in Portuguese. Chrome would pick by browser language, so the choice lives here instead.
